topArticle.title: LGBTQ+ people go into hiding in Senegal as hundreds are arrested
topArticle.description:
At least 320 people detained for ‘acts against nature’ after law criminalising homosexuality toughened, HRW reports
Mass arrests, forced HIV testing and barriers to legal representation are part of an escalating crackdown against LGBTQ+ people in Senegal, according to a new report.
More than 320 individuals have been arrested and detained on allegations of “acts against nature” since February, according to HIV Justice Network, an organisation quoted in the Human Rights Watch (HRW) report. Among these, at least 84 were charged with “voluntary HIV transmission”, solely on the basis of their HIV status.

The Zimbabwean writer Simbarashe Kundizeza has denied using AI to write a prize-winning short story after an article in the Atlantic said software had flagged it as almost completely AI-generated.
Kundizeza’s story The Blue Fighter was announced as the winner of the prestigious Caine prize for African writers on 6 October. Five days later, The Atlantic published an article by the author and journalist Vauhini Vara titled: “Yet Another Literary prize winner Seems to Be AI.”

The study, which would not investigate the safety or effectiveness of vaccines but would instead track “nonspecific” health outcomes like overall mortality or neurodevelopmental conditions, has been championed by Robert F Kennedy Jr, secretary of the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) and a longtime anti-vaccine activist.

As violent spirits are unleashed in Sky’s Possession, observers see confident creatives reclaiming the island’s narratives in a form of ‘cultural reparation’   
A woman opens a 300‑year‑old box, unleashing a violent spirit – it is the spirit of colonialism and oppression roaring back to life. It is a pivotal scene in Sky’s supernatural series Possession and symbolises a wider shift in Jamaica’s film industry, where directors are increasingly using the landscape to tell Jamaican stories – including those that confront enslavement, trauma and historical memory.
The series is about a biracial British lawyer who travels to Jamaica to investigate a multimillion-pound inheritance dispute, only to uncover a dark, vengeful spirit tied to the plantation’s brutal colonial past.

topArticle.summary: フィリピンで2022年にタマネギ価格が高騰し、最低賃金を超える価値になった問題で、「タマネギカルテル」に2800万ドルの罰金が科された。

topArticle.title: Australian woman charged with lacing colleague's curry with snail poison
topArticle.description: The alleged victim, who was in a relationship with the woman, had spotted bright green pellets in the meal.
topArticle.titleJa: オーストラリア人女性、同僚のカレーにカタツムリ毒を混入させた容疑で起訴
topArticle.summary: オーストラリアで、ある女性が交際相手だった同僚のカレーにカタツムリ駆除剤を混入させたとして起訴された。被害者は食事中に明るい緑色の粒を発見していた。

topArticle.title: Desperate to clear toxic haze, Indonesia douses its skies with dry ice
topArticle.description: Authorities in South East Asia have turned to weather modification as fires blanket the region in smog.
topArticle.titleJa: 有毒な煙害除去に必死、インドネシアが空にドライアイス散布
topArticle.summary: 東南アジア地域を覆う煙害を除去するため、インドネシア当局は空にドライアイスを散布する気象改変に着手した。

topArticle.title: North Korea and China open new bridge after 12-year delay
topArticle.description: China is the North's largest trading partner and a lifeline against the sanctions Pyongyang faces.
topArticle.titleJa: 北朝鮮と中国、12年遅れで新橋開通
topArticle.summary: 北朝鮮と中国を結ぶ新たな橋が12年の遅れを経て開通した。中国は北朝鮮最大の貿易相手であり、制裁下にある同国にとって生命線である。

topArticle.title: WTO and multilateral partners review progress on supply chain finance initiative
topArticle.description: Director-General Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala joined leaders of multilateral development banks and other international organizations at a high-level roundtable held on the sidelines of the 2026 World Bank – International Monetary Fund (IMF) Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Thailand, on 16 October to review progress in expanding supply chain finance in developing economies and to discuss priorities for the next phase of cooperation.
topArticle.titleJa: WTOと多国間パートナー、サプライチェーン金融イニシアチブの進捗状況をレビュー
topArticle.summary: 2026年10月16日、バンコクでのIMF・世界銀行年次総会の傍ら、WTO事務局長と多国間パートナーが開発途上国におけるサプライチェーン金融拡大の進捗状況を評価し、今後の協力の優先事項を協議しました。

topArticle.title: Talks kick off for Timor-Leste's accession to government procurement pact
topArticle.description: At a meeting of the Committee on Government Procurement on 14 October, parties to the Government Procurement Agreement (GPA) 2012 welcomed Timor-Leste's submission of key documents required to kick off its negotiations on acceding to the Agreement. The Committee also reviewed regulatory developments, heard updates on the accession process of other members, and for the first time conducted a dialogue with the private sector on the significance of the Agreement in a changing trade environment.
topArticle.titleJa: 東ティモール、政府調達協定加盟に向けた交渉を開始
topArticle.summary: 10月14日、政府調達委員会で東ティモールが政府調達協定への加盟交渉開始に必要な重要文書を提出し、歓迎されました。委員会は規制動向も検討し、民間部門との対話も初めて実施しました。

topArticle.title: Madagascar launches safeguard investigation on certain confectionary
topArticle.description: On 12 October 2026, Madagascar notified the WTO’s Committee on Safeguards that it had initiated on 9 October 2026 a safeguard investigation on imports of sugar confectionary as well as chocolate and cocoa confectionary.
topArticle.titleJa: マダガスカル、特定の菓子製品に対するセーフガード調査を開始
topArticle.summary: 2026年10月12日、マダガスカルは砂糖菓子、チョコレート菓子、ココア菓子の輸入に対するセーフガード調査を10月9日に開始したことをWTOセーフガード委員会に通知しました。
